source: Windows itself, as Microsoft documents it: the Known Folders and CSIDL references, the folders Windows Setup creates under %SystemRoot%, the files Windows ships there, the services and named pipes Windows' own components install and open, the streams Windows writes, the registry keys and values every installation holds, the object manager's namespaces, and the Task Scheduler task-definition schema. Nothing here is about one sample, family or run; each list states the criterion that admits an entry. Written for this project, not copied from a third-party table.
about: Host values every Windows system holds or every program may use, which a value the analysis states is refused as: an indicator on one matches every host. Compared case-insensitively, a path with '/' read as '\\' and each component with trailing dots and spaces trimmed (Windows ignores them). A component is a known folder when it is in 'known_folders' or 'environment_folders' (a multi-component entry of 'known_folders' as that sequence), is a form of 'system_roots' where a path starts or right after a drive, is in 'system_folders' within the chain such a form starts, begins with a 'known_folder_prefixes' entry, is a drive, is the profile name after 'Users', or is the 8.3 short name Windows generates for a known folder (its first six letters without spaces, a tilde and a digit). 'generic_names' are not refused: such a value is exported with a note that it may match ordinary software, and never becomes a matcher on its own.

known_folders.criterion: A folder Windows names as a known folder (Known Folders / CSIDL) outside %SystemRoot%, by its display or file-system name, or a folder Windows creates under one on every installation. An entry of more than one component counts only as that sequence of components: 'Microsoft\Windows', which Windows creates under the roaming and local application data and ProgramData known folders to hold the Start Menu, Programs, Startup, Templates, SendTo, Recent, Cookies, History and the Internet caches, per user and for all users. The folders of the %SystemRoot% chain are 'system_folders'.
known_folders.source: Microsoft Known Folders and CSIDL documentation.

known_folder_prefixes.criterion: The prefix of every CSIDL and KNOWNFOLDERID constant name.

environment_folders.criterion: An environment variable Windows defines on every installation that stands for a known folder.

system_folders.criterion: A folder Windows Setup creates in the %SystemRoot% chain on every installation, in which Windows keeps its own programs, drivers and data files. It counts as a known folder only in that chain: right under the system root ('system_roots') or under another folder of the chain, so a 'Drivers' or 'Tasks' folder anywhere else is a folder of its own.
system_folders.source: The %SystemRoot% layout of a clean Windows installation as Microsoft documents it (System, System32 and SysWOW64 with the WOW64 redirector's Sysnative, and their sub-folders wbem, drivers\\etc, WindowsPowerShell\\v1.0, spool, Tasks, config, catroot, downlevel; Fonts, INF, WinSxS, servicing). A folder any user or program writes in (Temp, Logs, Debug) is not one.

system_roots.criterion: How a path names %SystemRoot%, the folder the system chain starts at: the folder's own name and the environment forms Windows defines for it. A form counts only at a path's start or right after a drive, so a 'Windows' folder anywhere else is a folder of its own.
system_roots.source: Microsoft 'Recognized environment variables' documentation (SystemRoot, windir, SystemDrive) and the Windows folder a clean installation creates at the system drive's root.

system_binaries.criterion: A program, library or data file Microsoft ships as part of Windows, in the base image or as an optional Windows feature, in a currently supported Windows client or server release, listed for the folder of the %SystemRoot% chain Windows installs it to; Windows' own processes are among them (the session manager, the logon and service processes, the shell and the hosts they start). It is refused written bare or under the system folders alone (a drive allowed); anywhere else, or misspelt, it is a copy out of place and kept.
system_binaries.source: The files Microsoft ships in System32, SysWOW64, their sub-folders and %SystemRoot% itself in the supported Windows 10 and 11 releases (Long-Term Servicing Channel included) and Windows Server releases, with those the optional Windows features install there (Telnet and TFTP clients, Windows Subsystem for Linux, Credential Guard's isolated LSA, WMIC), as Microsoft's Windows documentation and its 'Features removed or no longer developed' lists describe them, and the processes Microsoft documents a running Windows to start from there.

object_namespaces.criterion: A namespace of Windows' object manager a named kernel object (a mutex, an event, a pipe) is created under; refused as a whole name, and read past when a name is checked for being generic.
object_namespaces.source: Microsoft 'Kernel object namespaces' documentation (Global, Local, Session) and the named-pipe file-system root.

windows_streams.criterion: An NTFS alternate data stream Windows itself writes or every file has.
windows_streams.source: Microsoft documentation of the default unnamed stream ($DATA), the Attachment Manager's Zone.Identifier, SmartScreen's and EFS's streams.

windows_services.criterion: A service Microsoft ships as part of Windows, installed by default or by an optional Windows feature or role, in a currently supported Windows client or server release, by its service (key) name; a service another product adds is not one.
windows_services.source: Microsoft 'System services for Windows' documentation and the Services key of a clean installation.

windows_pipes.criterion: A named pipe Windows' own services open (the well-known RPC pipes), in a currently supported Windows client or server release, by default or with the optional Windows feature that provides the service.
windows_pipes.source: Microsoft's protocol documentation of the well-known RPC named pipes ([MS-RPCE], [MS-SRVS], [MS-WKST], [MS-SAMR], [MS-LSAD], [MS-RRP], [MS-SCMR], [MS-TSCH], [MS-EVEN], [MS-RPRN]).

registry_keys.criterion: A registry key every Windows installation has, without its hive. A key under the Services key named after a Windows service is one too.
registry_keys.source: The registry layout of a clean installation as Microsoft documents it (Run keys, Explorer and shell-folder keys, Winlogon, Services, Control).

registry_values.criterion: A registry value Windows itself sets on every installation, as its key without the hive and the value name.
registry_values.source: The values a clean installation holds under the keys above, as Microsoft documents them (Explorer\Advanced view settings, Winlogon's Shell and Userinit, UAC's policy values, the machine GUID, the product name).

task_definition_words.criterion: An element or value name of the Task Scheduler task-definition schema, which every task carries.

generic_names.criterion: A word that is itself used, whole, as the name of a file, folder, scheduled task or service by many unrelated programs (the vocabulary of updaters, services, launchers and caches); a value named by one alone may match ordinary software.
generic_names.source: Common naming of Windows software components; no sample's names.

dotnet_framework_folders.criterion: A folder of the .NET Framework that Windows installs in the %SystemRoot% chain (Microsoft.NET, Framework, Framework64 and the version folders Windows ships), counted only in that chain like 'system_folders'.
dotnet_framework_folders.source: The .NET Framework installation layout under %SystemRoot%\\Microsoft.NET as Microsoft documents it for the versions Windows includes (2.0/3.5 and 4.x).

dotnet_framework_tools.criterion: A tool the .NET Framework installs in its version folders on every installation that includes it; refused only in that folder chain, like 'system_binaries'.
dotnet_framework_tools.source: The tools of a .NET Framework version folder as Microsoft documents them.

submission_roots.criterion: A folder a submitted file is placed in before it runs, by a sandbox or by a user: the temporary folders, the desktop, the downloads folder, the profile folder itself and a drive's root, by name and by the environment form Windows defines for it. The sample's submitted name is refused bare, directly under one of these, directly under a drive's root or directly in a profile folder ('Users\<name>'); under any other folder it is a copy the sample made and kept.
submission_roots.source: Microsoft Known Folders (Desktop, Downloads, the profile) and the TEMP, TMP and USERPROFILE environment variables; a drive root.
